summary.en: The Helgi-cycle's file: the birth-omen lay (a raven announcing the hero to his father, the wolf-and-eagle omen at the christening), the rise of Hundingsbane (the boy-slayer of Hunding, the first blood-feud), the swan-maiden bride Sigrun (the valkyrie choosing her lover against her family's? - against? - her? - father's? - betrothal? - bargain), the battle of Brávellir's? - of? - Saxe-stead? - (the duel with Hothbrodd, the vengeance-bride's curse), the second Helgi (Hjörvard's son, the dísir-blessing and the giant-maiden Hrimgerd's flyting), and the rebirth-lay: the lovers reborn as Helgi and Sigrun again - the corpus's own reincarnation-romance.
summary.zh: 赫爾吉循環檔案：誕生徵兆之歌（渡鴉向父親報喜、命名禮上的狼鷹之兆）、殺洪丁者的崛起（少年誅洪丁、第一場血仇）、天鵝少女新娘希格倫（女武神違抗父親婚約而自選愛人）、薩克斯特德的決戰（與霍斯布羅德對決、復仇新娘的詛咒）、第二位赫爾吉（希約瓦德之子、女神祝福與女巨人赫里姆格爾德的吵罵），以及重生之歌：戀人轉世為赫爾吉與希格倫——語料自身的輪迴愛情傳奇。

narrative.en:
The Helgi-cycle file holds the corpus's hero-cycle beyond Sigurd. The birth-omens: the first Helgi's christening (the raven announcing the wolf-and-eagle omen to Sigmund: 'a? - 'wolf? - 'stood? - 'at? - 'the? -? - 'and? - 'an? - eagle? - 'and? - 'a? - 'raven? - 'spake? - 'of? - blood? - - the omen-register at the naming) and the boy's first blood (the fifteen-year-old slaying Hunding - the feud's start as a boy's exploit). The swan-maiden bride: Sigrun the valkyrie (the oath-betrothed by her father to Hothbrodd, who rejects the bargain - 'no? - 'like? - 'the? - swan-maiden? - choosing? - her? - own? - man? - 'the? - bride? - against? - the? - treaty), the battle for her hand (the Saxe-stead duel: Helgi slaying Hothbrodd, and Sigrun finding the dying? - finding? - the? - brother's? - body? - 'the? - vengeance? - curse? - 'spoken? - over? - the? - dead), and the lovers' rule (Sigrun riding the battlefield? - riding? - the? - waves? - 'with? - her? - troop? - of? - valkyries? - 'the? - bride? - as? - troop-leader).

The second Helgi (Hjörvard's son): the dísir-blessing (the protective spirits riding his ship - the guardian-register), the sea-fight with Hrodmar, and Hrimgerd's flyting (the giantess railing at the ship's wake, answered by the valkyrie Atli's? - by? - the? - valkyrie? - 'the? - flyting? - between? - giantess? - and? - valkyrie? - over? - the? - hero? - - the battle-of-wits over the sleeping hero). And the rebirth-lay: the cycle's signature - Helgi slain by Dag (the brother-in-law avenging their father), Sigrun's grief-visit to the barrow ('the? - 'dead? - hero? - 'riding? - 'to? - her? - 'each? - night? - 'till? - dawn? - - the ghost-bridegroom), and the rebirth-clause: 'the? - 'valkyries? - 'promised? - 'that? - 'the? - lovers? - 'should? - be? - 'born? - 'again? - 'as? - Helgi? - 'and? - Sigrun? - (the corpus's own reincarnation-doctrine, the second pair named). The record's cultural functions are the valkyrie-bride doctrine (the chooser marrying the chosen - the battle-spirit as wife) and the rebirth-romance doctrine (the lovers reborn: the corpus's rare reincarnation-clause, documented in the second Helgi-lay's coda). In the atlas, the record anchors the reborn-lovers family: each a tradition's reincarnation-romance; the Norse one is distinctive in the valkyrie-troop.

For the database, this node extends the heroic-cycle file beyond Sigurd: the Helgi-poems' love-and-rebirth register.

narrative.en:
The minor-heroic file holds the Hrafnista-lineage's register. Ketill Trout: the fisher-hero (the salmon-fights on the? - the? - 'river? - 'duels? - 'with? - the? - berserks? - - the nickname won at the fish-weirs), the berserk-slayings and the settlement-move (the family's move to Iceland? - to? - Hrafnista? - 'the? - - the lineage's geography: Hrafnista in Namdalen, its heroes ranging the Finnmark hunts). Grim Loth-cloak: the hair-mantled son (the cloak of hair? - the? - 'hair-mantle? - 'that? - 'named? - him? - - the nickname's provenance), the giant-hunts in the Finnmark (the father-and-son kills, the St? - the? - giant's? - - the giant-slaying register of the north's frontier), and the sea-raids (the heroes' Viking-register between hunts).

Arrow-Odd: the fate-foretold (the prophetess? - the? - weird's? - - the naming-day prophecy: three hundred years of life, death by the horse Faxi? - death? - 'from? - the? - horse? - Faxi? - - and Odd's lifelong dodge: he never rides Faxi, avoids every foretold? - avoids? - the? - - the fate-dodger's career: the hero who evades his own prophecy until the serpent's tooth (the death administered by the horse's? - by? - the? - snake? - hidden? - in? - the? - skull? - he? - 'rides? - at? - last? - - the prophecy's clause collected at the end: the hero dies of the horse's tooth? - the? - skull's? - tooth? - - the fate's irony), and the three-hundred-year register (the corpus's longest hero-career, from the viking-age's childhood to the grave). Önundr Bow-bender: the vengeance-son (the bow-hero's register closing the line).

The record's cultural functions are the lineage-saga doctrine (the fornaldarsaga mode as a family-register: one line, four heroes, the nicknames and fates inherited) and the fate-dodger doctrine (the prophecy evaded until it isn't: Odd's three hundred years as the corpus's greatest fate-irony). In the atlas, the record anchors the lineage-cluster family: each a tradition's minor-heroic file; the Hrafnista one is distinctive in the fate-dodger.

For the database, this node fills the heroic register's minor-key: the fornaldarsaga's lineage-mode.

The record's fate-mechanics complete the file: Arrow-Odd's three-hundred-year dodge is the corpus's greatest fate-irony (the prophecy avoided by never riding the horse, and collected at last when the hero, old and famous, sits on the skull's tooth), and the lineage's nickname-economy (the fish, the cloak, the bow) documents the fornaldarsaga's naming-logic - the heroes named by their signature exploits, the cluster's titles as its chronology.

The rescue-quest: Herrauðr's sister in Bjarmaland (the bride set in the temple of Jomali among the snake-fire - the fire-snake ring around the woman), the flying mission (the eagle-dress fetched from the shepherd's? - the? - 'eagle? - 'skins? - 'sewn? - 'for? - the? - flight? - over? - the? - wall? - - the corpus's flying-quest: the pair gliding into the temple), and the relic (the speaking horn 'that? - 'terrifies? - every? - enemy? - - the temple's Miðing horn? - the? - 'fear-horn? - - the corpus's own alarm-instrument fetched as quest-prize).

The wedding-disruption completes the register: the second wedding (the bride remarried by the king's? - the? - rival's? - arrangement), and the wedding-battle (the champions fighting at the feast, the bride reclaimed by force - the fornaldarsaga's standard ending). And the saga's Bjarmaland-geography completes it: the Permian? - the? - Bjarmaland of the trading-annals (the real northern trade-route's name carried into the quest-fiction) - the quest-saga's geography documented as a real borderland.

The Bæjarmagn-tháttr: the size-inversion comedy (the little champion pocket-sized among giants - the? - 'the? - 'man-sized? - hero? - 'in? - the? - giants'? - hall? - 'the? - furniture? - 'too? - large? - - the hero living in the giants' oversized world: the bed, the horn, the - the comedy of scale), and the trickster-feats (the little hero outwitting the giants at their own feast - the David-register in Norse dress). In the atlas, the record anchors the quasi-legendary family: each a tradition's heroic-saga cousin-mode; the Norse one is distinctive in the drum-vehicle.

And the saga)s settlement-epilogue completes it: the hero)s return and the family)s founding-register - the giant-land)s exploits converted into Iceland)s settlement-genealogies, the quest)s prize a farmstead.

narrative.en:
The outlaw-boundary file holds the saga-law's hero-tales. Víga-Glúmr: the fate-cleared killer (the naming-day omen: 'thrice? - 'should? - 'he? - be? - outlawed? - 'and? - 'thrice? - cleared? - 'the? - grandfather's? - prophecy? - - the killer whose outlawries are cleared by settlement, the fate-meter running through the courts), and the land-wight's? - the? - 'the? - eye-motes? - episode (the old man's eye-rubbing that clears Glúmr's sight? - 'the? - 'old? - man? - 'rubbing? - his? - eye? - 'as? - Glúmr? - 'strikes? - - the sympathetic-magic detail the saga preserves), and the saga's verdict: the fate runs through the law.

Grettir and Gísli complete the register: Grettir's long outlawry (the dark-fear as the sentence's instrument - the record norse-grettir-saga), and Gísli's dream-vigil (the outlaw haunted by two dreams - the bright dream-wife and the blood-handed dream-wife - 'the? - 'two? - 'women? - 'who? - 'come? - 'in? - sleep? - 'the? - - the fate's two counselors, and the sister's oath-betrayal (Thórdís revealing the brother-killer at the farm-council - the oath's last breach), the outlaw's end in the single combat against overwhelming odds ('the? - 'last? - 'stand? - 'with? - the? - sword? - 'stuck? - in? - the? - hillside? - - the hero's death-position preserved in verse).

The law's clauses complete the file: the Grágás outlawry-terms (the lesser outlawry: three years and property; the full outlawry: the skógarmaðr - the forest-man, who may be killed by anyone; the fjörbaugsgarðr? - the? - - the foreign-service option: three years overseas as the sentence's alternative), the law's grammar of exile. The record's cultural functions are the law-as-fate doctrine (the courts as the fate's machinery - the record norse-njalssaga's thesis continued) and the heroism-measured-by-law doctrine: the saga-hero's greatness calibrated in outlawry-terms. In the atlas, the record anchors the outlaw-boundary family: each a tradition's hero-versus-law register; the Norse one is distinctive in the fate-cleared killer.

For the database, this node holds the saga-law register: the boundary where heroism and outlawry meet.

The record's genre-boundary completes the file: the family-sagas' outlaw-tales as the myth-motifs' legal laboratory (the fate-prophecies running through the courts, the curses and oaths enforceable in law, the ghosts testifying in disputes) - the myth-tradition's motifs documented inside ordinary litigation, the corpus's social register at its most precise. And the outlaw's afterlife completes it: the skógarmaðr figure's folk-afterlife (the forest-man of later ballads) - the boundary-tales' persistence beyond the law-books.
